title: Not Airtight
text:
Not Airtight. Note: There are several products attached to this listing. I am specifically writing this review for the 10-lb./5 L. container.

I selected this container initially with the idea of keeping my wife’s popcorn in it. She loves her popcorn and so far we have not had a good way to store it. Because she likes pre-popped popcorn for the convenience, this container seemed like a good solution for her, allowing her better access than bags and should seal better. I found this not to be the case – this container is not air-tight and does not seal as well as I’d hoped.

I will start with one thing about this container that seems a little counter-intuitive at first. The lid has a handle and the lid seals when the handle is down. This seems a bit backward at first – I expected the lid to seal with the handle up for carrying. However, this is a good arrangement because the container is designed for stacking, and when I considered that it made more sense. It’s not a design problem at all when considered in that way. With 10 pounds of rice in the container, the handle likely would strain under the weight anyway.

This is a generous sized container and it can hold quite a bit. It’s sufficient for storing most dry goods, like rice, popcorn, flour, sugar, and coffee beans.

My issue with this container isn’t the design but the implementation. To be blunt, the lid does not seal tightly. Even when “locked” with the handle down, and after watching the locking mechanism move the gasket, it is very easy to simply pop the top off, with very little resistance. Depending on what you’re sealing in and why will determine if this is good or bad. On one hand the seal is sufficient to keep out insects and other contaminants, but it is not enough to keep the contents free of humidity and certainly not sufficient to keep the lid secure if the container is dropped. So, if what you’re putting in has a tendency to get stale when exposed to moisture, this might not be the best solution.

This is a nice container that holds a lot, but it doesn’t seal as nicely as it should and that can be a real issue depending on what’s inside. For rice, it’s probably just fine when in a dry area, but for things like flour and sugar it’s probably going to disappoint.
